CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks being special means being better than other people.

example.question: What does it mean that you are God's special creation?
example.wrong_answer: You are better than other children
example.correct_answer: God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: The word special is heard as a prize or a rank.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "You are better than other children" beside "God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Say that every child is special in the same way, and ask each child to name one thing that makes a classmate special.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Everyone is God's special creation. Being special does not make you better than others, because God made them with love too.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks a person is a chance event, without a plan or a maker.

example.question: According to Psalm 139:13-14, how did God make you?
example.correct_answer: He knit you together, fearfully and wonderfully made

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: Science lessons and talk about birth leave out God as the maker.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "By chance, with no plan" beside "He knit you together, fearfully and wonderfully made" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Read Psalm 139:13-14 slowly and ask who is doing the knitting.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Psalm 139:13-14 says that God formed each person and that we are fearfully and wonderfully made. You were not made by chance.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks God made only the first people, Adam and Eve, not each person today.

example.question: Who made you, according to the Bible?
example.wrong_answer: God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only
example.correct_answer: God, who made every person in his image

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: The creation story is told as a story of long ago only.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only" beside "God, who made every person in his image" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Link Genesis 1:27 ("God created mankind in his own image") to Psalm 139:13 about each person.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Genesis 1:27 says God made human beings in his image, and Psalm 139:13 says he formed each of us. God is the maker of every person, including you.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks that feeling angry is itself a sin.

example.question: What does Ephesians 4:26 say about anger?
example.correct_answer: Do not sin when you are angry

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.cause: The child hears only the warning about anger.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.reveals: Offer "Never feel angry at all" beside "Do not sin when you are angry" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.help: Read the verse: it says "in your anger do not sin". Ask what the angry child can do instead of hitting or shouting.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says "in your anger do not sin". Anger is a feeling that comes to everyone. The wrong is in what we do with it.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks you should keep anger inside until you can get even.

example.question: What should you do about anger, according to Ephesians 4:26?
example.wrong_answer: Keep it and pay the person back later
example.correct_answer: Settle it before the sun goes down

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.cause: Revenge looks like justice to a hurt child.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.reveals: Offer "Keep it and pay the person back later" beside "Settle it before the sun goes down" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.help: Role-play saying sorry or forgiving before bedtime.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says do not let the sun go down while you are still angry. Settle it quickly by forgiving or talking, not by planning to pay back.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks we rejoice only when everything is going well.

example.question: What does Philippians 4:4 tell us to do?
example.wrong_answer: Rejoice only when things go well
example.correct_answer: Rejoice in the Lord always

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.cause: Joy is mixed up with having what we want.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.reveals: Offer "Rejoice only when things go well" beside "Rejoice in the Lord always" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.help: Ask whether we can be thankful to God even on a hard day, and why.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: Philippians 4:4 says "Rejoice in the Lord always". Our joy rests on God, who does not change, and not only on good days.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.error: Thinks a choice has no result if nobody sees it.

example.question: Kamau takes a pencil that is not his and nobody sees. What is true?
example.wrong_answer: There is no result because nobody saw
example.correct_answer: It still has results: he did wrong and he knows it

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.cause: The child links wrong only to being caught.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.reveals: Offer "There is no result because nobody saw" beside "It still has results: he did wrong and he knows it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.help: List the results of one choice: for the child, for the owner, and before God.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: Every choice has a result, even a secret one. Taking what is not yours is wrong whether or not anyone sees.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.error: Thinks the right choice is whatever friends are choosing.

example.question: Your friends tell you to skip class. How do you choose what to do?
example.correct_answer: Choose what pleases God, even if my friends choose differently

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.cause: Wanting to belong is stronger than wanting to be right.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.reveals: Offer "Do what my friends do" beside "Choose what pleases God, even if my friends choose differently" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.help: Role-play a polite NO and walking to class.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: A right choice is guided by the word of God, not by what the group does. Choose to obey and attend, even when friends choose differently.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.error: Thinks only big decisions are choices.

example.question: Which of these is a choice a child makes?
example.wrong_answer: Only deciding which school to attend
example.correct_answer: What to say, who to play with and whether to obey

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.cause: The child links choosing with grown-up decisions.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.reveals: Offer "Only deciding which school to attend" beside "What to say, who to play with and whether to obey" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.help: Make a list of the choices in one school morning.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: We make many choices every day: what to say, whom to sit with, whether to obey. Small choices matter too.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks being made in God's image means looking like God in face or skin colour.

example.question: What does it mean that people are made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27)?
example.wrong_answer: People have the same face as God
example.correct_answer: People are like God in being able to love, think and choose good

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: The word image is used at home for a photograph, so the child pictures a face.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "People have the same face as God" beside "People are like God in being able to love, think and choose good" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Show a photo and then a kind act: we show God's image by how we love, not by our faces. Every skin colour carries God's image.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: God's image is not about faces or colour. Everyone, of every look, is made like God to love and do good.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Reads "do not let the sun go down" as a rule about the weather or bedtime, not about ending anger quickly.

example.question: What does "do not let the sun go down while you are still angry" (Ephesians 4:26) teach?
example.correct_answer: Settle your anger the same day; do not keep it overnight

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.cause: The child takes the picture word by word.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.reveals: Offer "Go to bed before sunset" beside "Settle your anger the same day; do not keep it overnight" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.help: Ask: what happens at sunset? The day ends. So the verse says end your anger before the day ends.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: The verse is not about bedtime. It means make peace the same day and do not carry anger into tomorrow.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.error: Thinks what happens after a choice is luck, not a result of the choice.

example.question: Achieng did not study and failed her test. Why did she fail?
example.correct_answer: Her choice not to study had a result

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.cause: The child has heard adults blame luck and does not link the choice with what follows.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.reveals: Offer "Bad luck" beside "Her choice not to study had a result" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.help: Draw two arrows from one choice to its result. Ask the child to finish three such pairs.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: It was not luck. Not studying was a choice, and failing was its result.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Mixes the nuclear and the extended family.

example.question: Who belongs to the extended family?
example.correct_answer: Grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Only mother, father and children" beside "Grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Draw a small circle for the home and a bigger circle around it for relatives.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: The nuclear family is parents and their children. The extended family includes grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins too.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks family means only the people living in the same house.

example.question: Who counts as your family?
example.wrong_answer: Only those who live in my house
example.correct_answer: Those I live with and relatives who live elsewhere

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Many children see relatives rarely, and forget they are family.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Only those who live in my house" beside "Those I live with and relatives who live elsewhere" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Ask the child to name a relative who lives far away and how they keep in touch.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: Your family includes relatives who do not live with you, such as a grandmother in the village. They are family even if you see them rarely.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks honouring parents is only for when they give us things or agree with us.

example.question: When should a child honour his parents, according to Ephesians 6:1-3?
example.wrong_answer: Only when they give me what I want
example.correct_answer: Always, because it is right

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Honour is mixed up with a bargain.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Only when they give me what I want" beside "Always, because it is right" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Read Ephesians 6:1-3 and note the word "right" and the promise at the end.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: Ephesians 6:1-3 says to obey and honour your parents because this is right, and that it brings a good life. Honour does not depend on gifts.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks a child must keep a secret when an adult asks for it.

example.question: An adult touches you in a way that feels wrong and says "keep it a secret". What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble
example.correct_answer: Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: The child fears trouble or is told to be quiet.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble" beside "Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Say clearly: a secret about touching is never to be kept. Practise telling a teacher or parent.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: A wrong touch is never a secret to keep. Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult, such as a parent or teacher, or call Childline Kenya on 116.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks only strangers can hurt a child and that people we know are always safe.

example.question: Who might touch a child in a wrong way?
example.correct_answer: Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Warnings about strangers hide that harm can come from known people.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Only strangers" beside "Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Teach the rule: private parts are private, whoever asks.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: Anyone can do wrong, even a person we know. The rule is that private parts are private. If anyone breaks it, say NO and tell a trusted adult.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks it is the child's fault if he or she is touched wrongly, so there is no need to tell.

example.question: A child was touched wrongly. Whose fault is it?
example.wrong_answer: The child's fault, so she should say nothing
example.correct_answer: Never the child's fault, and she should tell

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Shame and fear stop a child from telling.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "The child's fault, so she should say nothing" beside "Never the child's fault, and she should tell" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Say it slowly: it is never your fault. Name the adults who will believe and help.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: It is never the child's fault. The person who touched wrongly did wrong. Tell a trusted adult, and keep telling until someone helps.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks honouring parents means doing anything an adult says, even something wrong or unsafe.

example.question: An adult relative tells you to steal from a shop. Does honouring your family mean you must do it?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, I must obey every adult
example.correct_answer: No: honour parents, but never do wrong; tell a trusted adult

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Honour and obey are taught together, so the child thinks any instruction must be followed.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Yes, I must obey every adult" beside "No: honour parents, but never do wrong; tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Ephesians 6:1 says obey parents "in the Lord": in what is right. Practise saying no politely to a wrong request.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: We honour our parents, but we never do wrong because someone tells us to. Say no and tell a trusted adult.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks a child need not tell if the wrong touch happened only once or the person said sorry.

example.question: A person touched you wrongly once and said sorry. Should you still tell a trusted adult?
example.correct_answer: Yes, always tell a trusted adult

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: The child wants to keep the peace and thinks one time is too small to report.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "No, it was only once" beside "Yes, always tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Repeat the rule with no exceptions: say no, go away, tell. Name three trusted adults the child could tell.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: Always tell a trusted adult, even if it happened once and even if the person said sorry.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.error: Thinks God made the world together with others or that others made parts of it.

example.question: Who made everything, according to Genesis 1?
example.correct_answer: God alone

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.cause: Stories from other places mention many makers.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.reveals: Offer "God and other gods together" beside "God alone" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.help: Read Genesis 1:1 and count how many makers are named.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.feedback: Genesis 1 shows God as the sole creator. He alone made the heavens, the earth and everything in them.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.error: Thinks God loves only children who are good.

example.question: What does 1 John 4:7-8 say about God?
example.wrong_answer: God loves only the children who are always good
example.correct_answer: God is love

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.cause: A child learns that bad behaviour is punished and thinks love is the same.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.reveals: Offer "God loves only the children who are always good" beside "God is love" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.help: Read "God is love" and ask whether love is a reward.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.feedback: 1 John 4:8 says "God is love". He is a loving Father to every child, and his love does not depend on being good all the time.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.error: Thinks holy means big, old or far away.

example.question: What does holy mean when we say God is holy?
example.correct_answer: Perfect and set apart, without sin

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.cause: The word is not used in daily speech.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.reveals: Offer "Very big and old" beside "Perfect and set apart, without sin" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.help: Link it to 1 Samuel 2:2: there is no one holy like the Lord.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.feedback: Holy means set apart and perfect, without any sin. 1 Samuel 2:2 says there is no one holy like the Lord.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.error: Thinks God is mainly angry and waiting to punish, so a loving Father cannot also be holy.

example.question: Can God be both holy and a loving Father?
example.wrong_answer: No, a holy God is only angry
example.correct_answer: Yes: God is holy and God is love

CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.cause: The child pictures a stern ruler and cannot hold two attributes together.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.reveals: Offer "No, a holy God is only angry" beside "Yes: God is holy and God is love" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.help: Put the two words side by side, holy and love, and read 1 Samuel 2:2 and 1 John 4:8. God is both at once.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.feedback: God is holy and God is love, both at the same time. He is a Father who knows you by name.
CRES.G4.CREATI.ATTRIBUTES_OF_GOD.ATTRIBU.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_HO.THE_INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD..error: Puts a New Testament book in the Old Testament.

example.question: Which book is in the Old Testament?
example.correct_answer: Genesis

CRES.G4.THE_HO.THE_INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD..cause: The child knows the names but not the two parts.
CRES.G4.THE_HO.THE_INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD..reveals: Offer "Matthew" beside "Genesis" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_HO.THE_INSPIRED_WORD_OF_GOD..help: Draw the Bible in two halves and sort book names on cards.

CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.help: Make a list of ways to help at home, school and church.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.feedback: We help with food, with work, with a visit and with a kind word, as well as with money.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.error: Thinks we help so that others will praise us.

example.question: Why should a Christian help the needy?
example.wrong_answer: So that people will praise me
example.correct_answer: Because of love for God and for others

CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.cause: Prizes and praise at school teach children to want a reward.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.reveals: Offer "So that people will praise me" beside "Because of love for God and for others" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.help: Ask whether Jesus helped for praise.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.feedback: A Christian helps out of love for God and for others, and not to be praised.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.error: Thinks a child can wait to help until it is convenient, though Matthew 5:42 says give to the one who asks.

example.question: A classmate has no pencil for the test and asks you. What does Matthew 5:42 teach?
example.wrong_answer: Help after the test if I remember
example.correct_answer: Give or lend now, to the one who asks

CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.cause: The child puts his own comfort first and does not see delay as refusing.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.reveals: Offer "Help after the test if I remember" beside "Give or lend now, to the one who asks" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.help: Act it: the test starts now. Help that comes later is no help.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.feedback: Matthew 5:42 says give to the one who asks. Help when the need is there.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.HELPING_THE_NEEDY.HELPING.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: How many silver coins did the woman have before she lost one?
example.correct_answer: Ten

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..cause: The nine that were left are remembered.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..reveals: Offer "Nine" beside "Ten" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..feedback: The woman had ten silver coins and lost one, so nine were left (Luke 15:8).
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..error: Thinks the woman soon gave up.

example.question: What did the woman do about the lost coin?
example.wrong_answer: She gave up because she had nine more
example.correct_answer: She lit a lamp and searched until she found it

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..cause: Children give up when something is small.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..reveals: Offer "She gave up because she had nine more" beside "She lit a lamp and searched until she found it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..help: Read Luke 15:8 and note "until she finds it".
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..feedback: The woman lit a lamp, swept the house and searched carefully until she found the coin. God likewise searches for the lost.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..error: Reads the parable as a lesson about money.

example.question: What does the parable of the lost coin teach?
example.correct_answer: God searches for the lost and rejoices when a sinner repents

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..cause: The story is about a coin.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..reveals: Offer "Count your money carefully" beside "God searches for the lost and rejoices when a sinner repents" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..help: Read Luke 15:10 for Jesus' own meaning.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..feedback: Jesus said there is rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:10). The coin stands for a person God loves.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..error: Thinks the woman kept the good news to herself.

example.question: What did the woman do when she found the coin (Luke 15:9)?
example.wrong_answer: Hid it and told no one
example.correct_answer: Called her friends and neighbours to rejoice with her

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..cause: The child thinks of money as private.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..reveals: Offer "Hid it and told no one" beside "Called her friends and neighbours to rejoice with her" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..help: Read Luke 15:9-10 and link it: the party on earth is like the joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..feedback: She called her friends to celebrate. Heaven rejoices like that when one person turns back to God.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_LOST_COIN..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..error: Thinks God's kingdom started big and mighty.

example.question: How does God's kingdom begin, in the parable of the mustard seed?
example.wrong_answer: With a very big and powerful start
example.correct_answer: Very small, like a seed, and then it grows

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..cause: People expect God's kingdom to be grand at once.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..reveals: Offer "With a very big and powerful start" beside "Very small, like a seed, and then it grows" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..help: Plant a seed in the school compound and watch.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..feedback: Jesus said the kingdom of God is like a mustard seed that grows into a tree (Luke 13:19). It starts small and grows.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

example.question: What happened to the birds in the parable?
example.correct_answer: They perched in the branches of the tree

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..cause: The child brings an idea of birds eating seed from farm life.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..reveals: Offer "They ate the seed" beside "They perched in the branches of the tree" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..feedback: Luke 13:19 says the birds perched in the branches of the tree. The kingdom gives shelter to many.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..error: Thinks only pastors or adults can help the kingdom of God grow.

example.question: Who can help God's kingdom grow?
example.correct_answer: Every Christian, including children

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..cause: Church work is seen as grown-up work.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..reveals: Offer "Only pastors and adults" beside "Every Christian, including children" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..help: List what a child can do: pray, be kind, invite a friend to church.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..feedback: Every believer can help the kingdom grow by praying, living well and telling others about Jesus.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..error: Thinks the parable is a lesson about growing mustard on a farm.

example.question: What is the parable of the mustard seed about (Luke 13:18-19)?
example.correct_answer: How God's kingdom grows from a small beginning

CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..cause: Parables use farm pictures, and the child stays with the picture.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..reveals: Offer "How to plant mustard" beside "How God's kingdom grows from a small beginning" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..help: Ask Jesus' own question first: "What is the kingdom of God like?" The seed is a picture of the kingdom.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..feedback: Jesus used a seed to teach about God's kingdom, which starts small and grows big.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.PARABLE_OF_THE_MUSTARD_S..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..error: Thinks Nicodemus came to Jesus in the daytime.

example.question: When did Nicodemus come to Jesus?
example.wrong_answer: At noon, in front of everyone
example.correct_answer: At night

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..cause: The child does not remember the detail.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..reveals: Offer "At noon, in front of everyone" beside "At night" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..feedback: John 3:2 says Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. He was a Pharisee and a member of the ruling council.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..error: Thinks Jesus meant being born a second time from a mother.

example.wrong_answer: To be born a second time from one's mother
example.correct_answer: A new life from God by water and the Spirit

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..cause: Nicodemus himself asked this in John 3:4.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..reveals: Offer "To be born a second time from one's mother" beside "A new life from God by water and the Spirit" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..feedback: Jesus was speaking of a new life from God, being born of water and the Spirit (John 3:5). Nicodemus first thought of a second birth from a mother.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..error: Thinks God loves only some people.

example.question: Whom does God love, according to John 3:16?
example.correct_answer: The whole world

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..cause: The child thinks the Bible stories are about one nation.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..reveals: Offer "Only the Jews" beside "The whole world" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..feedback: John 3:16 says God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes may have eternal life.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..error: Thinks baptism is only a water ceremony and changes nothing in how a person lives.

example.question: Why is baptism important to Christians today?
example.wrong_answer: It is only a nice ceremony with water
example.correct_answer: It shows a person has turned to God and begins a new life as a follower of Jesus

CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..cause: The child has seen a baptism as an event and not heard what it stands for.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..reveals: Offer "It is only a nice ceremony with water" beside "It shows a person has turned to God and begins a new life as a follower of Jesus" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..help: Link John 3:5 with Acts 2:38: repent and be baptised. Baptism marks a new life; ask what changes after.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..feedback: Baptism shows that a person has turned to God to live a new life following Jesus.
CRES.G4.THE_LI.NICODEMUS_ENCOUNTER_WITH..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.error: Thinks Joseph refused only because he feared his master.

example.question: Why did Joseph refuse, according to Genesis 39:9?
example.wrong_answer: He was afraid of his master
example.correct_answer: It would be a sin against God

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.cause: The child gives a fear of people as the reason.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.reveals: Offer "He was afraid of his master" beside "It would be a sin against God" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.feedback: Joseph said he could not do such a wicked thing and sin against God (Genesis 39:9). He feared God more than people.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

example.question: What did Joseph do when she held on to his cloak?
example.correct_answer: He left the cloak and ran out of the house

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.cause: The child thinks bravery means staying.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.reveals: Offer "He stayed to argue" beside "He left the cloak and ran out of the house" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.feedback: Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his cloak behind (Genesis 39:12). Sometimes the right thing is to run away from a bad situation.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.error: Thinks it is safe to do wrong when no one else is there.

example.question: Joseph was alone with her in the house. What was his reasoning?
example.wrong_answer: No one is here, so no one will know
example.correct_answer: God sees, so it is wrong even when no one else is there

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.cause: Children learn that wrong is only wrong if seen.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.reveals: Offer "No one is here, so no one will know" beside "God sees, so it is wrong even when no one else is there" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.feedback: Joseph knew that God sees. He refused even though no one else was in the house (Genesis 39:11).
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.error: Thinks a stranger who offers sweets or a lift is safe because he is kind.

example.question: A stranger offers you sweets and a lift home. What should you do?

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.cause: The child confuses kindness with safety.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.reveals: Offer "Accept, because he is kind" beside "Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.help: Role-play a firm NO and walking to a shop, a teacher or a parent.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.feedback: A stranger who offers gifts or a lift is not safe. Say NO, go away at once and tell a parent or teacher.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.error: Thinks every adult can be trusted to take a child anywhere.

example.question: Which of these is a trusted person for a child?
example.wrong_answer: Any adult who tells me to come
example.correct_answer: My parent, my teacher or a church leader I know

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.cause: Children are taught to obey adults.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.reveals: Offer "Any adult who tells me to come" beside "My parent, my teacher or a church leader I know" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.help: List trusted people by name, and the rule that a trusted person never asks for a secret.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.feedback: Trusted people are those who care for you and are known to your family, such as parents, teachers and church leaders. Not every adult is trusted.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.error: Thinks a child should not report because nobody will believe or help.

example.question: Whom can you report to if you are in danger?
example.wrong_answer: No one, they will not believe me
example.correct_answer: A parent, a teacher, the chief or Childline Kenya on 116

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.cause: Fear and shame stop a child from reporting.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.reveals: Offer "No one, they will not believe me" beside "A parent, a teacher, the chief or Childline Kenya on 116" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.help: Say the list aloud and practise telling.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.feedback: You can tell a parent, a teacher, a church leader, the chief or Childline Kenya on 116. Keep telling until someone helps.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.error: Thinks trusting God means no trouble will come.

example.question: What does it mean to trust in the Lord, according to Psalm 125:1?
example.correct_answer: To stand firm like Mount Zion, even in trouble

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.cause: The child hears trust as a promise of an easy life.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.reveals: Offer "Nothing bad will ever happen" beside "To stand firm like Mount Zion, even in trouble" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.help: Read Psalm 125:1 and ask what Mount Zion does when the wind blows.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.feedback: Psalm 125:1 says those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion which cannot be shaken. Trouble may come, but God holds us.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.error: Thinks that trusting God means doing nothing ourselves.

example.question: Wanjiru trusts God to help her in an exam. What fits?
example.wrong_answer: She does not study, she just prays
example.correct_answer: She studies and prays

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.cause: Trust and work are set against each other.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.reveals: Offer "She does not study, she just prays" beside "She studies and prays" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.help: Remind: the servants in the parable used what they had.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.feedback: Trusting God does not mean doing nothing. We do our part and trust God with the rest.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_L.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.error: Thinks the strength of Mount Zion comes from us.

example.question: Why can those who trust in the Lord not be shaken?
example.wrong_answer: Because they are strong in themselves
example.correct_answer: Because God stands by them

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.cause: The child thinks the verse praises human strength.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.reveals: Offer "Because they are strong in themselves" beside "Because God stands by them" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.help: Read Psalm 125:1-2 and ask who surrounds the people.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.feedback: Psalm 125 says the Lord surrounds his people. Their firmness comes from God.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_O.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.error: Thinks Joseph was rewarded at once for doing right.

example.question: What happened to Joseph soon after he refused Potiphar's wife?
example.wrong_answer: He was made a ruler at once
example.correct_answer: He was lied about and put in prison

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.cause: The child expects good to be rewarded straight away.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.reveals: Offer "He was made a ruler at once" beside "He was lied about and put in prison" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.help: Read Genesis 39:20 and then 41:41: doing right was costly first; God was with him in prison.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.feedback: Joseph did right and was put in prison at first. God was with him and later raised him up.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.JOSEPH_RESISTS.M_C4.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.error: Thinks a person met on a phone or online is a trusted person because they know the child's name.

example.question: Someone online knows your name and school and asks to meet. Is that a trusted person?
example.correct_answer: No: tell a parent or teacher and do not meet

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.cause: Knowing a name sounds like knowing the person.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.reveals: Offer "Yes, they know me" beside "No: tell a parent or teacher and do not meet" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.help: Make two lists: people I know and trust at home, school and church; people who only know about me.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.feedback: Knowing your name does not make someone safe. Tell a parent or teacher and never go to meet them.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.SAFE_PEOPLE.M_C4_SP.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_Z.error: Thinks Psalm 125:1 is only about a mountain in Israel and not about people who trust God.

example.question: In Psalm 125:1, who is like Mount Zion?
example.correct_answer: Those who trust in the Lord

CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_Z.cause: The child keeps the place name and misses the comparison.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_Z.reveals: Offer "Only the city of Jerusalem" beside "Those who trust in the Lord" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CHRIST.TRUST.TRUST_GOD.M_C4_TG_Z.help: Read the verse in two halves: "Those who trust in the Lord / are like Mount Zion". Ask what the first half is about.

example.question: About how many people joined the believers that day?
example.correct_answer: Three thousand

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.cause: Small numbers are more familiar to children.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.reveals: Offer "Twelve" beside "Three thousand" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.feedback: About three thousand people were added that day (Acts 2:41).
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.error: Thinks Acts 2:38 asks only for baptism with no change of life.

example.question: What did Peter tell the people to do first, in Acts 2:38?
example.correct_answer: To repent, and be baptised

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.cause: The child remembers the ceremony and forgets the turning.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.reveals: Offer "Only to be baptised" beside "To repent, and be baptised" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.help: Read the verse and note the first word, repent.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.feedback: Peter said "Repent and be baptised". To repent is to turn away from sin.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.error: Thinks every disciple was a fisherman.

example.question: What was Matthew's work before he followed Jesus (Matthew 10:3)?
example.correct_answer: A tax collector

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.cause: The best-known call stories are of fishermen.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.reveals: Offer "A fisherman" beside "A tax collector" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.help: Read Matthew 10:3 and 9:9. Make two groups: fishermen (Peter, Andrew, James, John) and Matthew the tax collector.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.feedback: Not all were fishermen. Matthew was a tax collector before Jesus called him.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.TWELVE_D.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.error: Places the start of the church in Rome or Antioch instead of Jerusalem.

example.question: In which city did the church begin on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2)?
example.correct_answer: Jerusalem

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.cause: The child knows other famous church cities from later lessons.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.reveals: Offer "Rome" beside "Jerusalem" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.help: Read Acts 2:5 ("staying in Jerusalem") and mark Jerusalem on a map. Antioch comes later.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.feedback: The church began in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.CHURCH_B.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.error: Thinks Stephen asked God to punish those who stoned him.

example.question: What did Stephen pray for those stoning him?
example.correct_answer: That God would not hold this sin against them

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.cause: Revenge is expected of a hurt person.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.reveals: Offer "That God would punish them" beside "That God would not hold this sin against them" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.feedback: Stephen prayed "Lord, do not hold this sin against them" (Acts 7:60). He forgave, as Jesus did.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.error: Says believers were first called Christians in Jerusalem, where the church began, instead of Antioch (Acts 11:26).

example.question: In which city were believers first called Christians?
example.correct_answer: Antioch

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.cause: Jerusalem is the city most known in Acts.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.reveals: Offer "Jerusalem" beside "Antioch" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.help: Find Antioch on a Bible map.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.feedback: Acts 11:26 says that at Antioch the believers were first called Christians.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.error: Thinks it is fine to join a group that does not follow Jesus if friends do.

example.question: Your friends join a group that mocks Jesus. What should you do?
example.correct_answer: Politely refuse and stand firm in your faith

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.reveals: Offer "Join them to fit in" beside "Politely refuse and stand firm in your faith" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.feedback: Stephen stood firm even when it cost him dearly. We should not join groups that do not follow Jesus, but refuse politely and stay firm.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.error: Forgets that Saul was there, holding the coats, when Stephen was stoned.

example.question: Who looked after the coats of the men who stoned Stephen (Acts 7:58)?
example.correct_answer: A young man named Saul

CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.cause: The child does not yet know Saul, who became Paul.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.reveals: Offer "Peter" beside "A young man named Saul" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.help: Read Acts 7:58 and say: this Saul later became the apostle Paul.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.feedback: A young man named Saul held their coats. Later God changed him and he became Paul.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.STANDING_FIRM_IN_FAITH.ST.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.error: Thinks "daily bread" means asking for riches or only bread.

example.question: What do we ask for when we pray "Give us today our daily bread"?
example.correct_answer: What we need each day

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.reveals: Offer "Riches for ever" beside "What we need each day" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.help: Ask what a child needs each day: food, clothes, health.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.feedback: In the Lord's Prayer, "daily bread" means what we need each day. We ask God to provide.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.error: Thinks we may ask for forgiveness without forgiving others.

example.question: What does the Lord's Prayer say about forgiveness?
example.wrong_answer: Forgive us, and we need not forgive others
example.correct_answer: Forgive us as we forgive others

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.cause: The second half is left out.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.reveals: Offer "Forgive us, and we need not forgive others" beside "Forgive us as we forgive others" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.feedback: The Lord's Prayer says "forgive us our debts as we also have forgiven our debtors" (Matthew 6:12). We forgive others too.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.error: Thinks Christians pray only at church or once a week.

example.question: When should we pray?
example.correct_answer: Every day, at home and anywhere

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.reveals: Offer "Only at church" beside "Every day, at home and anywhere" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.help: Make a list of times: morning, meals, bedtime.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.feedback: Jesus taught us to pray. We can pray every day, at home, at school and at church.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.error: Thinks "your kingdom come" asks for a country or a king to rule Kenya.

example.question: What do we ask for when we pray "your kingdom come"?
example.wrong_answer: For a new king to rule Kenya
example.correct_answer: That God's rule and will be done on earth as in heaven

CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.cause: The child knows kingdom as a land with a king.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.reveals: Offer "For a new king to rule Kenya" beside "That God's rule and will be done on earth as in heaven" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.help: Read the next line too: "your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven". The kingdom is God's rule in people's lives.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.feedback: "Your kingdom come" asks that God's will be done on earth as in heaven.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_PRAYER.LORDS_P.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..error: Thinks the fruit of the Spirit are real fruits like mango or banana.

example.question: What are the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23?
example.correct_answer: Love, joy, peace, patience and others

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..cause: The word fruit means food to a child.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..reveals: Offer "Mangoes and bananas" beside "Love, joy, peace, patience and others" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..help: Say that fruit here means what grows in a person's life.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..feedback: The fruit of the Spirit are qualities such as love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..error: Puts a work of the flesh, such as jealousy, in the list of the fruit of the Spirit.

example.question: Which of these is a fruit of the Spirit?
example.correct_answer: Kindness

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..cause: Sorting good from bad is quick but slips.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..reveals: Offer "Jealousy" beside "Kindness" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..help: Sort cards into fruit and not fruit.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..feedback: Kindness is a fruit of the Spirit. Jealousy and anger are not.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..error: Thinks the fruit of the Spirit show only in church.

example.question: Where should the fruit of the Spirit show?
example.correct_answer: Everywhere, at home, school and church

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..reveals: Offer "Only in church" beside "Everywhere, at home, school and church" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..help: Give examples at a football game.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..feedback: The fruit of the Spirit show in the whole of life, at home, at school, at play and at church.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..error: Thinks there are only five fruit of the Spirit, the number learnt in Grade 3.

example.question: How many fruit of the Spirit are named in Galatians 5:22-23?
example.correct_answer: Nine

CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..cause: Grade 3 asked for five, so the child thinks five is the whole list.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..reveals: Offer "Five" beside "Nine" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..help: Count them on the fingers from the verse: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..feedback: Galatians 5:22-23 names nine: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.FRUIT_OF_THE_HOLY_SPIRIT..source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.error: Thinks self-control means doing whatever one feels like.

example.question: What is self-control?
example.correct_answer: Choosing what is right instead of what my feeling pushes me to do

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.reveals: Offer "Doing whatever I feel like" beside "Choosing what is right instead of what my feeling pushes me to do" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.help: Role-play counting to ten when angry.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.feedback: Self-control means choosing what is right even when a feeling pushes us another way.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.error: Thinks self-control comes only from our own strength.

example.question: Where does self-control come from, according to Galatians 5:22-25?
example.correct_answer: It is a fruit of the Holy Spirit

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.cause: The word control sounds like effort.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.reveals: Offer "Only from my own strength" beside "It is a fruit of the Holy Spirit" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.feedback: Self-control is a fruit of the Spirit. We ask for the Spirit's help and keep in step with him (Galatians 5:25).
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.error: Thinks drugs or harmful videos are fine if done in secret.

example.question: A friend offers you a harmful video to watch in secret. What shows self-control?
example.wrong_answer: Watch it, since no one will know
example.correct_answer: Refuse and keep your mind and body clean

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.cause: Secrecy seems to remove the harm.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.reveals: Offer "Watch it, since no one will know" beside "Refuse and keep your mind and body clean" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.help: Ask what harm comes even if nobody finds out.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.feedback: Things that harm the body and mind are wrong even in secret. Self-control means saying no.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.error: Thinks trying something harmful once does no harm.

example.question: A friend says "just try one cigarette, once is nothing". What does self-control say?
example.correct_answer: No: say no every time

CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.cause: The child thinks harm comes only from doing something often.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.reveals: Offer "Once is fine" beside "No: say no every time" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.help: Explain that habits start with once, and practise saying no politely but firmly.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.feedback: Self-control means saying no even to the first time.
CRES.G4.THE_CH.SELF_CONTROL.SELF_CONTROL.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.error: Thinks an online stranger who is friendly can be trusted.

example.question: A stranger online asks to chat in private and meet. What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Chat and meet, he is friendly
example.correct_answer: Not reply, and tell a parent or teacher

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.cause: The child cannot tell who is really online.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.reveals: Offer "Chat and meet, he is friendly" beside "Not reply, and tell a parent or teacher" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.help: Say that people can lie about who they are.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.feedback: People online may not be who they say. Do not chat with strangers or agree to meet them. Tell a parent or teacher.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.error: Thinks it is safe to share passwords and the home address.

example.question: Which should you keep private online?
example.correct_answer: My password and home address

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.reveals: Offer "My favourite song" beside "My password and home address" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.help: List what a stranger could do with a password.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.feedback: Keep your password and home address private. Sharing them can let others harm you or use your account.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.error: Thinks it is fine to do wrong online if nobody will know.

example.question: You find a way to send an unkind joke about a classmate without your name. What shows integrity?
example.correct_answer: Do not send it, because it would hurt

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.reveals: Offer "Send it, nobody will know" beside "Do not send it, because it would hurt" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.feedback: Integrity means doing right even when no one is watching. An unkind message hurts whether or not your name is on it.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.error: Counts a non-digital object as a digital device.

example.question: Which of these is a digital device?
example.correct_answer: A mobile phone

CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.cause: Digital is confused with modern or useful.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.reveals: Offer "A pencil" beside "A mobile phone" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.help: Show a phone, a tablet and a pencil and ask which needs power and a screen.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.feedback: A digital device is one such as a phone, a tablet or a computer. A pencil is not a digital device.
CRES.G4.MORALI.USE_OF_SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher
